newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese construction, real estate shares rise.
newsitem.headline: Japanese construction, real estate shares rise.

text.p: Shares in the construction 0#CON.T and real estate 0#REA.T sectors rose in Tokyo on Thursday morning, bolstered by a newspaper report that the Japanese government may use public funds to buy land held by loan-collecting bodies.
As of 0046 GMT, the share price of Fujita Corp was up 14 yen or 7.78 percent at 194 yen, making it the biggest percentage gainer on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Aoki Corp, up 10 yen or 6.67 percent at 160 yen, ranking as the second-largest gainer.
At 0104 GMT, Hazama Corp, another construction firm, was up 19 yen at 268, ranking third.
Mitsubishi Estate Co Ltd, a major real estate firm, was up 90 yen at 1,400, ranking sixth.
Also, Tobishima Corp rose nine yen to 160 yen, Haseko Corp was up 12 yen at 215 yen, and Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd rose nine yen to 178 yen.

The Japanese financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Thursday that the Japanese government plans to use additional public funds to buy collateralised land formally owned by failed "jusen" mortgage companies and other troubled financial firms.
Comments from government officials were not immediately available.
